title: amendment
description:
The claimant adds evidence to a claim already filed. It never changes what was committed: the claim hash is the claim's identity and its address on chain, so a claim whose committed content changed would be a different claim at a different address, and every validation of the first one would be a judgement of something that no longer exists.

So an amendment is additive and separately signed. A validator that has already judged the claim can see exactly what arrived afterwards and decide whether to look again; one that has not can take the claim and its amendments together.

submission.description: Which amendment this is, counting from 1. The original claim is submission 0 and is not an amendment.

evidence.description: Evidence added, grouped the same way as the claim's. Ids must not collide with those already used by the claim or an earlier amendment.

detail.description: What this adds and why it was not in the original.
